sources.quote: Many friends, such as Will Rothenstein, the artist, Conder, who is a sort of Corot of the sunlight, Ernest Dowson, the poet, and others have come to see me for a few days: and next month I hope to see Ricketts and Shannon, who decorated all my books for me, dear Robbie Ross, and perhaps some others.
sources.context: Wilde to Carlos Blacker, 12 July 1897, Berneval-sur-Mer (MS Koch, Yale). The roll-call of who came after prison. Corot is the French landscape painter, and the compliment is to Conder's light.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That he came to Berneval, and what Wilde thought of his painting.
sources.provenance: PDF page 961; printed folio 911 confirmed on the rendered page image.

sources.quote: Conder is now a vineyard: the Youngs are very serious about him, and there is a moral atmosphere about Dieppe that you should come over and dissipate.
sources.context: Wilde at Berneval, August 1897, on the same printed page as the second Laurence Housman letter. 'A vineyard' appears to be a joke at the expense of some improving influence being exerted on Conder at Dieppe; the sense is not explained on the page and nothing is inferred.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: Conder in the Dieppe circle, and Wilde's tone about him.
sources.provenance: PDF page 978; printed folio 928 confirmed on the rendered page image.

name: Charles Conder
bio: Painter, celebrated for watercolours on silk and for painted fans. He was one of the friends who came out to Berneval to see Wilde in the summer of 1897, alongside Rothenstein and Dowson, and Wilde described him to Carlos Blacker as 'a sort of Corot of the sunlight'. He drew the landscape and figures on a picture postcard Wilde sent Leonard Smithers from Napoule at the end of 1898.
